title: Colony and Echo
premise: Oscar Villalobos is a clone of a murdered courier, running cargo and secrets along the silent corridor between the colony worlds of Meridian and Cael, whose war ended in stalemate and mutual silence. When a manifest lists a passenger aboard a ship that was destroyed years ago, Oscar finds a hidden message from his original — proof that the murder was ordered to bury a peace treaty both governments still fear. Pursued by intelligence officers from both sides, Oscar must choose between erasing himself forever and delivering the message that could end the war. He delivers it, at the cost of his own anonymity, and in doing so inherits not just the original's case but his unfinished family.
about_author: Marguerite Brightwater is the pen name of a former shipping-logistics analyst who spent a decade writing route reports before turning them into fiction. She lives near a decommissioned spaceport and writes about people who carry things for a living.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Establishes Oscar's life as a clone courier on the Meridian–Cael run: invisible by design, tolerated because he's useful. He delivers sealed messages he never reads and keeps a ritual of visiting the grave of his original. Emotional beat: loneliness worn like a uniform, and the quiet ache of being someone's copy.

chapters.title: A Name That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Processing manifests at Cael Station, Oscar finds 'E. Villalobos' listed on the Perihelion — a ship destroyed six years ago, the same ship his original died aboard. The manifest shouldn't exist; neither should the sealed cylinder attached to it. Emotional beat: dread curdling into obsession as the past reaches forward.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: POV Oscar, with flashback fragments. The cylinder contains a partial message from his original: coordinates, a warning about 'the third signature,' and evidence the murder was arranged by someone inside Meridian's peace ministry. Emotional beat: grief reframed as inheritance — the original left him work, not just a face.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Checks Manifests
chapters.summary: POV alternating Oscar and Ines Okonkwo, a Caeli customs officer who notices the impossible manifest too. Their first meeting is adversarial — she suspects him, he lies badly. Emotional beat: two lonely professionals recognizing each other's competence before they trust each other.

chapters.title: Runners in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Both governments' intelligence services flag the manifest anomaly. Ines covers for Oscar once, burning her clean record, and realizes she's chosen a side without meaning to. Emotional beat: duty beginning to crack against something warmer and more dangerous.

chapters.title: The Third Signature
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Following the original's coordinates to an abandoned relay station, Oscar decodes the full message: a verified peace accord, ready for ratification, buried because three officials — one from each world and one broker — profited from the war's frozen state. Emotional beat: fury and purpose fused; invisibility becomes impossible.

chapters.title: Everything We Were Told to Forget
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Ines is arrested and interrogated by her own service; she gives up nothing but learns the conspiracy reaches her mentor. Meanwhile Oscar, hunted, hides with a found-family network of independent couriers who owe his original debts. Emotional beat: belonging discovered in the margins — the family he never knew he had.

chapters.title: The Broker
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. The war-profiteering broker corners Oscar, offering him a new identity and total erasure in exchange for the message — the temptation of the oblivion he always wanted. Oscar refuses, understanding for the first time that he wants to be someone, not no one. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes; love against duty becomes love as duty.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV alternating, climax. With Ines freed by her courier allies, Oscar hijacks the old relay station to broadcast the accord simultaneously to both worlds — forcing ratification by making denial public. The broker's forces attack; Ines holds the line while Oscar transmits. Emotional beat: sacrifice, terror, and the exhilaration of finally mattering.

chapters.title: Colony and Echo
chapters.summary: POV Oscar, epilogue months later. The war ends not with celebration but with slow, awkward reopening of contact; the conspirators face tribunals. Oscar, now publicly known, chooses to keep flying the long route — with Ines as his partner and the courier network as family. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; the echo outlives the original, and that's enough.
